sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 02-01-2015 at about 12-00 p.m., the petitioner was driving the Auto bearing No.AP-03-TC-2029 from V Kote-Palamner road.

When he reached near RTC Bus stand, V Kota Town, at that time the driver of APSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.AP-11-Z-1846 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed against the Auto rickshaw in which petitioner was proceeding, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to PES Hospital, Kuppam, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
The petitioner has spent huge amount towards treatment.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was a driver and also doing agricultural work and thereby earning a sum of Rs.25, 000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.

He has suffered pain and sufferings,
permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. Respondent- the RC owner cum insurer of APSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.AP-11-Z-846 has filed the written statement and contended that there is no jurisdictional to try the matter.

It is further contended that the driver of APSRTC bus was driving the bus slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road from V Kota bus stand, at that time the driver of goods auto came from left side cross road and suddenly entered the main road, the driver of APSRTC bus after noticing the driver of auto entering the main road, suddenly took the bus to the left side and immediately stop the bus on the left side of the road , in spite of it the driver of auto without controlling his vehicle came and dashed against the front left body of the bus.
It is further contended that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of auto and that the petition is bad of non joinder of necessary parties .

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 02-01- 2015 at about 12-00 p.m., near RTC bus stand, on V Kota-Palamner road, Kajeepeta, V Kota Town,
Chittoor District, Andrapradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus bearing Reg.No.AP-11-A-1846 by its driver as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom ?
3. What Order or Award?

sentences.text: The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P12 and closed evidence on his side.
The respondent has not adduced any oral evidence.

7. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: in the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 9 Issue No.1 : - In order to prove the case and thereby to prove that rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of offending vehicle is the sole cause for accident, the petitioner has given evidence as PW.1.
It is deposed by PW.1 that on 02-01-2015 at about 12-00 p.m., he was driving the Auto bearing No.AP-03-TC-2029 from V Kote- Palamner road.

When he reached near RTC Bus stand, V Kota Town, at that time the driver of APSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.AP-11-Z-1846 (hereinafter referred to as the offending the vehicle) came from opposite direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Auto in which he was proceeding, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained,
treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P4 to Ex.P8 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint and translated copy of complaint, sketch, wound certificate, charge sheet etc.,
11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Raghavereddy, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 01/2015 of V. Kota Police Station for the offence punishable under section 337 IPC.

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.
146/196 MV Act and Sec. 3/181 MV Act.
12.
So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the sketch at Ex.P6 is perused, the accident in question has occurred on the left side of V Kota-Palamner road.
The offending vehicle was coming from opposite direction i.e., from Palamner towards Kuppam.
The petitioner was proceeding on the correct direction of the road i.e., on the left side of the road.
If the driver of the offending vehicle had driven his vehicle on the left side of Palamner - Kuppam road this accident would not have occurred.

Though the respondent has taken the contention that the driver of offending vehicle has not contributed any negligence but they have not taken any steps to substantiate the said contention by not examining the driver of offending vehicle.
It is true that there is delay of 4 days in lodging the complaint.
But on the date of accident itself the petitioner has taken treatment at PES Medical College on the history of RTA collusion between APRTC and auto Rickshaw.

Hence, the materials placed on record clearly prove that the driver of offending vehicle Janardhan Reddy Alias S. Janardhan vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82158895/
3 alone has contributed negligence.

sentences.text: Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.1 and Ex.P7.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at P.E.S Medical College Hospital, Bangalore from 02-01- 2015 to 21-01-2015 for a period of 20 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries.

14. Dr. Sahailesh A V Rao, Senior consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics is examined as Pw2 and through him OPD records from Padmashree Diagnostics and Neuro Psychologist report are got marked as Ex.P11 and Ex.P12.
P.W.2 has deposed that the petitioner consulted him at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore on 17-07-2024 and again on 25-07-2024 for the assessment of his disability.
The PW.2 further deposed that in the CT brain done to the petitioner, it revealed Right Frontal Intra Parenchymal bleed.
The PW.1 complains frequent headaches, giddiness, impaired memory and intelligence.
On examination revealed a conscious patient who Impaired Memory and Intelligence.
15. PW.2 further deposed that the neuro psychological assessment was done to the petitioner on 25-07-2024 and the petitioner obtained an IQ of 56 (90-109).
He is below average in thinking and reasoning.
On IDEAS, he obtained score 09 indicating moderate disability of 40-70%.
His MMSE score is 21/30 which is low score.
PW.2 further deposed that he has assessed the disability as per the disability Assessment and Certification Guidelines issued by DGHS, GOI during 2001 and 2018.
On the modified Rankin Scale, the petitioner has score of 1.
As per the guidelines, this amounts to a disability of around 20%.
16. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, admittedly he is not a treated doctor.
The petitioner has not undergone any surgery.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained abrasion injury of 2x2 cm and blood was oozing from ears.
The PW.2 except verifying the discharge summary has not verified the case sheet.

He has not verified any document for the follow up treatment if any taken by the petitioner and it is admitted by PW.2 that he was not present at the time of treatment given by the neurophysiologist and non of the document discloses the type of treatment given by neurophysiologist.

It is admitted by PW.2 that there is no document to prove that because of the head injury sustained by the petitioner it has adversely affected him and admitted that none of the medical documents discloses that the petitioner has headache and his memory power is lessened.

17. If the evidence of PW.1 is perused, he has given rational answer to the entire question posed to him without any hindrance even for a while and cleverly he has given answer to the entire question posed to him and it is he who himself has represented the case without his being represented through guardian.

Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment rendered in MFA No.9065/2019 c/w MFA No.3748/2019 between Raghugowda Vs. The Mangaing Director,
BMTC, wherein, in the similar set of facts the doctor has reported that petitioner has sustained 50%
disability but the court while observing that the petitioner has filed application on his own and as a normal person he has prosecuted the petition, he has given evidence on his own and he is a normal person with normal intellect has observed that petitioner has not suffered any disability and only Janardhan Reddy Alias S. Janardhan vs Apsrtc on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82158895/
4 with a view to get higher compensation, he has chosen to produce a false report and PW.2 being a responsible doctor has not only given a false report but also given evidence on oath based on such false report has decline to consider the percentage of disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 18. The observation made in the aforesaid ruling is aptly applicable to the case in hand.
Hence, this court declines to consider the evidence of PW.2 and intern declines to consider the neurological disability assessed by the PW.2.

When petitioner has sustained head injury and underwent surgery,
under such circumstances because of the head injury suffered by him it may have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort but not under the head loss of future income.
19. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
20. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
21. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, the petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.39,000/- as per Ex.P2 and medical receipt at Ex.P10.

As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.39,000/- under the head medical expenses.
22.

It is stated that petitioner was aged about 56 years and he was driver apart from doing agricultural work and thereby earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m. and due to the accident it could not possible to do his work and that on account of the injuries sustained by him he is getting pain every now and then which incapacitated him from doing the work as before the accident.
The petitioner has not proved his monthly income.

Hence this court inclines to consider the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.9,000/- p.m.
23.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 20 days as inpatient at P.E.S Medical College Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for 3 months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.27,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
24. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 20 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.

He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2015.

sentences.text: The petitioner at his age of 22 years has suffered permanent disability, hence definitely some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities and discomfort would have caused to the petitioner.
Hence he is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl

. No Heads Amount Rs.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 60,000/-
2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 3.

Towards loss of income during Rs. 27,000/-
 laid up period 4. Medical expenses Rs. 39,000/-
5. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.1,00,000/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,56,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Six Thousand only).
26.
As regarding liability is concerned, the Respondent being the RC owner cum insured of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent this court directs the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
27. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,56,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Six Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,56,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Six Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
